html:
For building muscle or "boosting growth hormone": no peptide is approved for that. Here is what the sold ones actually are.

No peptide is FDA approved for building muscle. Tesamorelin is approved for one specific use in people with HIV; growth hormone peptides sold for muscle are not approved.

  • Sermorelin · pharmacy-made growth-hormone shotNo FDA-approved product on the marketon prescription

    A pharmacy-mixed shot on prescription that makes the body release growth hormone. No approved product.

    A growth-hormone-releasing shot from compounding pharmacies; the approved brand was taken off the market years ago.

    No FDA-approved product on the market.

    Prescription through clinics.

    No listings yet
  • CJC-1295 / ipamorelin · vials sold for growth hormoneNot approvedresearch use only

    Peptides meant to release growth hormone, in research-use vials. Not approved, no large trials in people.

    Growth-hormone-releasing peptides sold by research-use shops and some clinics. No approved product, no large human trials.

    Not approved for any use.

    Research-use shops, with our checks.

    No listings yet
  • IGF-1 LR3 · vials sold for muscleNot approvedresearch use only

    A lab-made, longer-acting form of IGF-1 sold for muscle, in vials for lab use. Not approved.

    A modified form of IGF-1, a hormone the body makes in response to growth hormone. No approved product; the approved IGF-1 medicine, mecasermin (Increlex), is a different product. 401

    Not approved.

    Research-use shops, with our checks.

    No listings yet
  • Tesamorelin (Egrifta) · daily shot for belly fat in HIVFDA approvedon prescription

    A daily shot on prescription, approved only to reduce belly fat in people with HIV, not for muscle.

    A daily shot approved only to reduce belly fat in people with HIV. Sold off-label by clinics for "growth hormone".

    FDA approved for HIV-related belly fat only.

    Prescription.

    On prescription; no clinic prices yet
  • Testosterone (TRT) · gel or shot for low testosteroneFDA approvedon prescription

    A gel or shot on prescription. Approved only for men with low testosterone from a medical condition.

    Replaces a hormone the body makes too little of. Not FDA approved for low testosterone without an associated medical condition. 10

    FDA approved only for low testosterone with an associated medical condition.

    Prescription, after blood tests. Our testosterone page compares the online clinics that prescribe it.

    On prescription; no clinic prices yet
